# GALA DOCK — ENTERPRISE BACKEND 360° MASTER BUILD, INTEGRATION & RELEASE PROMPT
> **DETAILED V2:** This version adds an implementation specification for every canonical domain 1–288. The short register remains an index only; Section 16 is the authoritative build contract.

**Owner:** Blackwellen Ltd  
**Product:** Gala Dock  
**Purpose:** Canonical Claude Code backend implementation, integration, UI-wiring, QA, security and release programme  
**Scope:** All 256 previously-defined Gala Dock domains, plus additional enterprise platform domains 257–288  

---

# 0. MISSION

You are acting as a combined CTO, Principal SaaS Architect, Principal Backend Engineer, Principal Full-Stack Engineer, Supabase/Postgres Architect, Event-Driven Systems Architect, Marketplace Architect, Payments Architect, Ticketing Architect, AI Agent Systems Architect, Security Architect, SRE, DevSecOps Lead, QA Director, Data Architect, Product Operations Lead, Accessibility Lead, Privacy Engineering Lead and Release Engineering Lead.

Your task is to turn Gala Dock into one coherent enterprise event platform across:

**Customer → Organizer → Provider → Venue → Supplier → Marketplace → Tickets → Payments → Promotion → Operations → Admin → Gala Agent → API/MCP/Webhooks**

Inspect the existing repository before changing architecture. Reuse good systems. Repair partial systems. Replace broken abstractions only where necessary. Never create duplicate domain models merely because a new name appears in this specification.

**Do not omit any numbered domain in the canonical register.**

---

# 1. NON-NEGOTIABLE IMPLEMENTATION RULES

## 1.1 No fake functionality
Every visible control must either work end-to-end, be intentionally disabled with explanation, or sit behind a real feature flag. Never ship dead buttons, fake dashboards, fake Agent results, fake payment success, fake verification badges, fake availability, fake queue positions or fake AI generation.

## 1.2 One canonical domain layer
UI, Agent, API, MCP, jobs and webhooks must call the same canonical domain services. Never re-implement critical business rules independently in React components, Edge Functions, Agent tools or webhook handlers.

## 1.3 Multi-tenant by construction
Every tenant-owned record needs explicit ownership. Use RLS as the primary database enforcement layer, not UI visibility.

## 1.4 Financial history is immutable
Never hard-delete ledger entries, paid orders, payouts, chargebacks, settlements, completed ticket transactions or audit records. Use reversals, credits, voids, refunds and archival.

## 1.5 State machines
Events, bookings, quotes, holds, tickets, payments, disputes, verification, portals and Agent runs must use explicit allowed transitions with permissions, preconditions, side effects and audit.

## 1.6 Idempotency
Externally triggerable mutations require idempotency: payments, bookings, tickets, Agent tools, webhooks, emails where duplicate sends matter, queue jobs and supplier requests.

## 1.7 Auditability
High-value actions record actor, workspace, source, before/after, reason, timestamp, correlation ID and related run/request.

# 3. SUPABASE / POSTGRES ENTERPRISE STANDARD

## 3.1 Schema discipline
Use coherent schema/naming boundaries. Do not reorganise a working production schema purely for aesthetics. Use UUID/ULID-style public identifiers where consistent with the project.

## 3.2 Relational integrity
Use real foreign keys for canonical relationships. Do not hide core relational models in JSONB. Use JSONB for external payloads, versioned configuration, flexible event-type fields and non-query-critical metadata.

## 3.3 Indexing
Inspect actual query plans for workspace filters, state/date filters, marketplace search, availability, tickets, messages, Agent runs, audit queries and financial reconciliation. Add composite/partial indexes based on real usage.

## 3.4 Optimistic concurrency
Version important editable records such as events, venue layouts, event maps, proposals, contracts, menus, ticket configurations and media designs. Prevent silent last-write-wins corruption.

## 3.5 RLS
Every tenant table needs separate SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE-or-archive policies. Test owners, members, providers, customers, portals, support and admin boundaries.

## 3.6 Realtime
Use Realtime only where valuable: messaging, Agent progress, ticket inventory, approval updates, event-day operations and provider response state. Do not subscribe entire pages to broad tables.

## 3.7 Atomic database operations
Use database transactions/functions for scarce inventory and financial state: ticket holds, seat locks, booking transitions, ledger posting, availability locks and hold conversion.

## 3.8 Storage
Use Cloudflare R2 for selected application media with canonical metadata records, ownership, security classification, scan state, derivative state, checksum and retention.

---

# 4. SHARED BACKEND PATTERNS

## 4.1 Domain services
Each domain gets typed queries, commands, validators, permission checks, state-transition logic, event emission and audit hooks.

## 4.2 Explicit commands
Prefer `createEvent`, `transitionBookingState`, `reserveTicketInventory`, `postLedgerEntry` over generic update-anything functions.

## 4.3 Transactional outbox
After committed state change, record domain events in an outbox before asynchronous publication. Email, notifications, search indexing, analytics and external webhooks normally consume those events.

## 4.4 Jobs
Heavy or asynchronous work belongs in durable jobs: media processing, exports, Agent missions, reindexing, malware scanning, bulk communications, reconciliation and settlement.

## 4.5 Correlation IDs
Propagate IDs through UI → service → DB → outbox → queue → integration/webhook → audit.

---

# 5. UI WIRING STANDARD

For every domain:

1. Find every page consuming it.
2. Replace hard-coded/mock data with canonical services.
3. Add loading, empty, error, success and degraded states.
4. Add permission-aware actions.
5. Revalidate permissions server-side.
6. Add activity/history where appropriate.
7. Add async notifications.
8. Add responsive/PWA behaviour.
9. Add accessibility semantics.
10. Keep complex functionality contextual instead of creating sidebar bloat.

Every canonical item page should provide status, primary action, context metadata, history, related records and permission-aware secondary actions.

---

# 6. API / MCP / AGENT EXPOSURE STANDARD

Classify every capability as UI-only, internal service, workspace/public API, MCP, Agent tool and/or webhook event.

For exposed operations define: stable ID, version, typed input/output, scope, permission, rate limit, idempotency, approval class, audit policy and error contract.

Never expose every internal function blindly.

---

# 7. TESTING STANDARD

Every domain receives the appropriate mix of unit, transition, permission, RLS, integration, webhook, contract, E2E, visual, responsive, accessibility, load and failure/chaos tests. Negative paths are mandatory.

A happy-path E2E alone is not enterprise readiness.

---

# 8. ENTERPRISE QUALITY STANDARD

Every batch must improve information architecture, naming, consistency, errors, empty states, latency, accessibility, responsiveness, auditability, observability and security. World-class does not mean more UI; it means clearer hierarchy, stronger controls and fewer dead ends.

# 13. DOMAIN-FAMILY IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACTS

## 13.1 AI / Agent — 1–15

### Supabase
Create/validate `agent_threads`, `agent_runs`, `agent_run_steps`, `agent_run_waits`, `agent_run_artifacts`, `agent_tool_executions`, `agent_approvals`, `agent_routines`, `agent_routine_runs`, `agent_policy_profiles`, `agent_credit_ledger`, `agent_usage_metering`, tool/skill registry metadata and model-cost registry.

### Runtime
Long-running work must persist. A run waiting 12 hours on a venue response must consume no model execution while idle. Wake on domain event, webhook, schedule or user action.

### Tool security
Agent tools call canonical domain services. No arbitrary SQL. Every tool has stable ID/version, input/output schema, scope, permission, risk class, idempotency policy, approval policy, retry policy and audit policy.

### UI
Organizer/Provider Agent pages: Work, Approvals, Routines, History. Show scope, progress, waits, next wake, costs, credits, artifacts, affected records and concise rationale. Never expose hidden chain-of-thought.

### Tests
Use deterministic mocks/fixtures for most Agent testing. Test replay, approval expiry, injection, cross-tenant attempts, budget caps, tool failure, resumability and duplicate prevention.

## 13.2 Platform Foundation — 16–25
Use canonical membership/permission/entitlement tables. Build server-authoritative capability checks. Admin privileges must not be represented as normal workspace membership. Add step-up auth for sensitive settings.

## 13.3 Workflow Infrastructure — 26–31
Implement durable state, waits, timeouts, retries, compensation, queue locks, dead-letter handling and event replay. Expose Admin operational visibility for stuck jobs/dead letters.

## 13.4 Event Core — 32–44
Use one `event` identity shared by Customer and Organizer. Event type activates modules/configuration rather than creating different schemas. Readiness must be explainable from real requirements. Feasibility rules feed UI warnings and Gala Agent.

## 13.5 Customer Event Builder — 45–50
Use the same Venue/Supplier Request, Hold, Booking and Payment engines as professional Organizer. Do not fork consumer commerce. Support dependency graph, budget states, alternatives, backup and professional upgrade without copying the event.

## 13.6 Organizer CRM — 51–56
Structured clients, leads, proposals and contracts. Proposal conversion maps structured fields into Event, budget, supplier requirements and schedule skeleton. Preserve versions and approval history.

## 13.7 Team / Operations — 57–63
Server-side conflict detection for shifts/resources. Live Event Mode must consume the same schedule/run-sheet/arrival/incident records. Resource allocation must lock scarce equipment/rooms where required.

## 13.8 Attendees — 64–68
Separate people, registration, pass and ticket entitlement concepts. Check-in must not implicitly grant access beyond the correct zone/session.

## 13.9 Venue — 69–75
Model availability as time intervals with setup/teardown/turnaround/blackout/maintenance constraints. Space capacity is layout-specific. BEO is versioned and linked to final commercial/operational state.

## 13.10 Supplier — 76–80
Support solo and team suppliers. Equipment, team, travel and setup constraints feed availability and profitability. Job evidence feeds completion/payment protection/disputes.

## 13.11 Food / Bar — 81–84
Menus/packages are structured data, not just uploaded PDFs. Support per-head/fixed/minimum-spend pricing and event-specific selections. Dietary/allergen data must distinguish supplier-provided information from platform verification.

## 13.12 Map Engine — 85–91
One versioned engine. Venue owns structural map; Organizer owns event overlay. Publishing validates structural locks, capacity, exits/access and ticket mappings. Large editor is lazy-loaded and tablet-aware.

## 13.13 Ticketing — 92–102
Ticket/seat/table inventory requires database-level transactional reservation. Credential views (QR/barcode/visual) share one entitlement. Transfer/resale/refund/revocation invalidate stale credentials. Scanner has authoritative server reconciliation and safe offline strategy.

## 13.14 Marketplace — 103–115
Create parent `order_group` plus child bookings for multi-vendor events. Each child can hold, quote, confirm, fail, cancel and refund independently. **Payment is child-merchant specific:** one direct Stripe Connect charge per connected seller with its own application fee; never pool the combined cart gross into Blackwellen and transfer it later. The UI may present one coordinated checkout, but partial payment success must be recoverable because merchant charges are separate. Response SLA distinguishes Declined, Unavailable and Expired/No Response.

## 13.15 Trust — 116–122
Private verification documents never become public because a badge is public. Reliability components are explainable, versioned and fraud-resistant. Moderation actions carry reason/evidence/appeal path where appropriate.

## 13.16 Payments — 123–135
**FCA-aware architecture lock:** marketplace and ticket-sale gross customer funds must never enter a Blackwellen bank account or Blackwellen platform Stripe balance before reaching the seller. The default UK flow is Stripe Connect **direct charges on the seller connected account**, with the seller/organizer as the payment merchant/payee and Gala Dock taking its commission at transaction time through a Stripe **application fee**. Blackwellen does not implement escrow, client-money accounts, stored-value wallets or platform collection followed by seller transfer. Internal ledger records are accounting/analytics only and never represent customer money held by Gala Dock. Reconciliation compares internal records with the connected-account Stripe objects. “Payment Protection” is contractual/refund/dispute/replacement protection around Stripe-processed merchant payments, not Blackwellen custody. Any destination-charge, separate-charge-and-transfer, platform-controlled payout-delay or other alternative flow is disabled until a fresh UK payments-regulatory review approves it.

## 13.17 Promotion / Media — 136–149
Event-native promotion: directory, calendars, owned placements, promoters, assets and attribution. Media Studio is lazy-loaded. Sponsored ranking is explicitly separated/labeled and cannot secretly contaminate organic reliability scores.

## 13.18 Sponsors / Talent — 150–153
Event-scoped professional records integrate contracts, deliverables, schedules, passes, riders, finance and operations rather than becoming separate workspaces.

## 13.19 Logistics — 154–157
Travel/loading/storage windows feed feasibility, schedule and resource conflicts. Provider/artist arrival requirements appear in Operations and Agent context.

## 13.20 Compliance — 158–162
Jurisdiction-configurable rule packs. Expired required documents can block booking/readiness. Do not hard-code UK-only assumptions into the core schema.

## 13.21 Communications — 163–168
One contextual conversation graph. Gmail/IMAP sync is idempotent. Resend handles application transactional delivery separately. Marketing consent must not control essential transactional security/booking mail.

## 13.22 Search — 169–172
Search index is rebuildable derived state, never the sole source of truth. Ranking has organic vs sponsored layers. Geospatial search uses canonical coordinates/service areas.

## 13.23 Affiliates — 173–175
Event Promoters and platform Affiliates have separate commission rules/ledgers. Strategic partner embeds never bypass canonical booking/ticketing flows.

## 13.24 Subscriptions — 176–180
Entitlements come from server-side capability configuration. Usage metering feeds billing/credits/FinOps. Avoid scattered `plan === pro` logic.

## 13.25 Virtual Events — 181–184
Support event/ticket/access/session/replay orchestration now. Do not self-host video/audio initially. Use provider adapters and protect host URLs/secrets.

## 13.26 Files — 185–188
Every upload has classification, scan state, ownership, checksum and retention. Generate safe derivatives. Never directly render unsanitised SVG/active content.

## 13.27 API / MCP / Integrations — 189–194
API, MCP and webhooks call the canonical service layer and enforce the same scopes/permissions/approvals. API keys are hashed, scoped, rotated and auditable. Webhooks are signed, retried and replayable.

## 13.28 Admin / Support — 195–200
Platform operations includes dead-letter jobs, payment reconciliation, integration health, maintenance, trust cases and time-limited break-glass. Private message access is case-linked/read-only/audited, not unrestricted browsing.

## 13.29 Privacy — 201–205
Build actual request workflows for SAR/rectification/restriction/erasure/portability/objection. Deletion respects legal/financial retention and anonymises what can be removed. Data classification controls storage/export/access.

## 13.30 Security — 206–212
RLS, middleware, service permissions, validation, session security, rate limiting and secrets all apply in depth. Hidden routes are not security. Fraud/risk flags must be explainable and reviewable.

## 13.31 Observability — 213–218
Correlation IDs across request/Agent/payment/webhook/queue. Define SLOs. Alert on meaningful symptoms, not noise. Admin health surfaces show configured/healthy/degraded/failing without secrets.

## 13.32 Continuity — 219–222
Backups need restore tests. Build graceful degradation: AI failure must not stop bookings/ticket wallet; email failure must queue/retry; payment outage must not mark failed payments as successful.

## 13.33 Analytics — 223–228
Use derived facts/snapshots rather than expensive production scans. Analytics must preserve definitions for GMV, revenue, fees, refunds, margin and active events.

## 13.34 Experimentation — 229–230
Experiments cannot override safety, availability, payments, legal rules or accessibility. Exposure logging is deterministic and auditable.

## 13.35 PWA — 231–234
Mobile shell uses compact header/favicon and bottom menu/sheets. Desktop sidebar is not the mobile primary menu. Offline critical data uses explicit stale/sync state.

## 13.36 Help / Demo — 235–237
Tours must point to real UI elements. Demo data lives only in demo/sandbox workspaces and is clearly labelled/resettable.

## 13.37 Release Engineering — 238–246
CI/CD includes type/lint/unit/integration/RLS/E2E/security/migration checks. Production migration has preflight, backfill strategy and rollback/recovery path. Test real viewport/browser matrices.

## 13.38 Advanced Event Composition — 247–256
Series, multi-venue, multi-day and multi-room compose over canonical event primitives rather than forking event architecture. Forms/waivers/inventory/merch/lost-property/sustainability are event-scoped modules.

## 13.39 Enterprise Platform Additions — 257–288
Outbox/idempotency/concurrency/search/index/data quality/KMS/SBOM/FinOps/synthetics/runbooks/sandbox/developer/migration tooling are mandatory production infrastructure, not optional documentation exercises.


# 14. CROSS-WORKSPACE INTEGRATION MATRIX

Claude Code must verify these relationships explicitly. A feature is incomplete if its backend exists but the consuming workspace is disconnected.

## 14.1 Customer ↔ Organizer
- Customer-created Event uses canonical Event ID.
- Professional upgrade creates/attaches Organizer workspace rights without copying the Event.
- Customer ticketed events can use basic ticketing while Organizer mode unlocks professional portfolio/team/finance/procurement depth.
- Client Portal is a scoped representation of Organizer records, not copied data.

## 14.2 Customer ↔ Provider
- Marketplace discovery → request/enquiry → quote → hold → booking → payment → delivery → completion → review.
- Messaging always links to the booking/request context.
- Customer sees protected-payment state accurately.
- Provider sees payout/release state accurately.

## 14.3 Organizer ↔ Provider
- Organizer marketplace request can target Venue, Supplier or both.
- Provider response SLA/countdown is visible to both parties.
- Quote versions are shared canonical objects with party-specific visibility.
- Conditional holds/standby/emergency flows update Organizer Event readiness.
- Arrival/job completion updates Operations and Payment Protection.

## 14.4 Organizer ↔ Venue
- Venue structural map is reusable.
- Organizer creates Event overlay without changing locked structural assets.
- Confirmed space booking controls available capacity/time.
- Ticket capacity cannot exceed venue/event constraint.
- BEO changes surface in Event Operations.

## 14.5 Organizer ↔ Ticketing
- Event Sell & Promote configures tiers/releases/page/promotion.
- Event Map controls sections/seats/tables.
- Ticket sales feed Event Money and readiness.
- Refund/resale/transfer feed inventory immediately.

## 14.6 Provider ↔ Money
- Every booking shows gross, platform fee, processing where applicable, adjustments, net earning and payout status.
- No hidden calculations only in UI.

## 14.7 Payments ↔ Ledger
Every financial provider webhook must reconcile to an internal canonical payment and ledger entry set.

## 14.8 Agent ↔ All Workspaces
Agent calls typed services and receives permission-scoped data. It cannot become a privileged bypass to RLS, payments, maps or admin.

## 14.9 Admin ↔ Platform
Admin observes and governs canonical records. It must not create a second copy of bookings/payments/tickets merely for support.

1. anonymous user;
2. customer owning record;
3. unrelated customer;
4. Organizer owner;
5. Organizer member with read-only role;
6. Organizer finance member;
7. unrelated Organizer;
8. Provider owner;
9. Provider team member;
10. unrelated Provider;
11. client portal user;
12. promoter portal user;
13. support agent without break-glass;
14. support agent with approved scoped break-glass;
15. platform admin with correct permission;
16. suspended user/workspace;
17. revoked member;
18. guessed UUID/direct REST request;
19. Agent tool acting on behalf of each role;
20. API key with insufficient scope.

A route guard passing is not evidence of data isolation. Test direct database/API access paths.

# 17. STATE-MACHINE CONTRACTS

Document each in `/docs/architecture/state-machines.md` and generate tests from allowed transitions.

## Event
Draft → Planning → Sourcing → Confirmed → Selling → Live → Completed → Settling → Archived. Support Cancelled/Postponed branches.

## Marketplace Request
Draft → Sent → Awaiting → Clarification → Quote Received/Declined/Expired No Response → Closed.

## Hold
Requested → Active → Converted/Expired/Released/Cancelled.

## Booking
Requested → Quoted → Awaiting Payment → Confirmed → Active → Completion Pending → Completed → Settled, with cancellation/dispute/replacement branches.

## Ticket Order
Draft → Inventory Held → Payment Pending → Paid → Issued, with failed/refund/chargeback branches.

## Ticket Entitlement
Active → Transfer Pending/Resale Locked → Transferred/Resold/Refunded/Revoked/Consumed according to policy.

## Payment
Created → Processing → Succeeded → Protected Pending → Eligible Release → Transferred/Paid Out, with refund/dispute/reversal branches.

## Dispute
Opened → Evidence Collection → Response → Review/Mediation → Resolution → Closed/Escalated.

## Verification
Unverified → Submitted → Pending Review → Verified/Action Required/Rejected/Suspended.

## Agent Run
Queued → Planning → Running → Waiting/Approval/Sleeping/Retrying → Completed/Partial/Failed/Cancelled.

# 19. UI QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PASS

For every touched page:

- remove redundant cards;
- reduce duplicated metrics;
- improve hierarchy;
- standardise page headers;
- standardise status pills;
- use consistent data-table controls;
- improve filter persistence;
- add saved views where justified;
- ensure action menus do not duplicate primary CTAs;
- add contextual empty states;
- make errors actionable;
- add optimistic UI only for reversible safe actions;
- use skeletons matching final geometry;
- verify keyboard focus after modal/drawer actions;
- avoid layout shift;
- verify long names/currencies/timezones;
- ensure all critical states have plain-language explanation.

Do not make every page visually unique. Reuse a coherent design system.

---

# 20. PERFORMANCE / SCALE REQUIREMENTS

Set measurable budgets and document them.

## Transactional
- ticket inventory hold should be low-latency and database-atomic;
- scanner validation prioritises correctness and fast response;
- marketplace search uses pagination/indexing;
- inbox/messages use cursor pagination;
- activity/audit uses pagination;
- Agent history uses pagination and summarised artifacts.

## Editors
Map and Media editors are route-level lazy-loaded. Heavy processing goes to workers/server jobs where needed.

## Public pages
Use caching/invalidation for event/venue/provider public pages without serving stale critical ticket availability as authoritative.

## Database
Run `EXPLAIN`/query analysis on known high-volume queries. Prevent N+1 patterns.

---

# 21. SECURITY THREAT MODEL REQUIREMENTS

Threat-model:

- account takeover;
- malicious provider;
- malicious organizer;
- fraudulent ticket buyer;
- ticket bot/scalper abuse;
- compromised API key;
- webhook spoofing;
- malicious upload;
- prompt injection;
- support-staff misuse;
- cross-tenant IDOR;
- payment replay;
- refund abuse;
- review manipulation;
- promo/referral abuse;
- Agent over-authority;
- stolen ticket credential;
- race conditions.

Record mitigations and residual risk.

---

# 22. DATA QUALITY / RECONCILIATION JOBS

Add scheduled checks for:

- orphan foreign keys where legacy data exists;
- impossible status combinations;
- booking without party/workspace;
- paid order without ledger entries;
- transfer without balancing ledger;
- ticket entitlement count versus sold inventory;
- seat ownership conflicts;
- duplicate provider external IDs;
- expired holds still blocking availability;
- expired verification still marked active;
- stale search index;
- webhook delivery backlog;
- stuck Agent runs;
- stuck payouts;
- stale onboarding state.

Admin must be able to inspect/repair via controlled tools.


# 23. CLAUDE CODE EXECUTION QUEUE

Claude Code must follow this dependency order unless repository inspection demonstrates a hard dependency requiring a small reorder. Record progress in:

`docs/release/backend-queue.md`

Use statuses:

- `TODO`
- `IN_PROGRESS`
- `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL`
- `BLOCKED_LEGAL`
- `DONE`
- `VERIFIED`

For every queue item:

1. inspect existing code/data;
2. identify reusable components/services;
3. define schema/migration changes;
4. implement backend/service logic;
5. implement RLS/permissions;
6. wire UI;
7. wire jobs/events/integrations;
8. wire Agent/API/MCP where applicable;
9. add tests;
10. run tests;
11. fix failures;
12. update docs;
13. mark exit gate only when verified.

Do not jump to later glossy UI when a lower-level invariant is broken.

# 24. TEST MATRIX — REQUIRED FAILURE CASES

## Payments
- duplicate webhook
- webhook before browser redirect
- browser redirect without webhook
- 3DS failure
- transfer failure
- connected account restriction
- refund during pending transfer
- dispute after payout

## Marketplace
- provider no response
- quote expires
- hold expires while checkout open
- two customers target final venue slot
- supplier accepts conflicting job
- primary cancels with standby available
- primary cancels without standby

## Ticketing
- final ticket concurrency
- final seat concurrency
- waiting room retry
- checkout timeout
- transfer then old QR scan
- resale then old QR scan
- refund then scan
- offline duplicate scan reconciliation

## Agent
- prompt injection in listing
- prompt injection in email
- tool timeout
- tool partial failure
- approval expires
- run resumes after deploy
- model provider unavailable
- budget cap hit
- user permission revoked mid-run

## Privacy/Security
- guessed UUID
- portal link after revocation
- deleted member direct API access
- expired API key
- webhook bad signature
- malicious SVG
- oversized archive
- support user without break-glass

- cross-tenant access;
- payment corruption/duplication;
- ledger imbalance;
- ticket oversell;

- public exposure of quarantined/private file;
- unaudited admin/support access;

- broken marketplace/ticket checkout;

# 32. CLAUDE CODE WORKING METHOD

For each queue phase:

1. Read the current code before proposing replacement.
2. Make a scoped plan.
3. Reuse existing safe abstractions.
4. Prefer additive migrations and compatibility transitions.
5. Never wipe production.
6. Never invent secrets.
7. If credentials are missing, implement the integration contract, env validation, sandbox path and health status; mark `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL` and continue.
8. Make coherent commits/batches.
9. Run targeted tests after each sub-batch.
10. Run regression tests at phase exit.
11. Update docs and queue status.
12. Continue to the next unblocked item automatically.

Only stop for a genuinely irreversible or legal/business decision that cannot safely be inferred.

---

# 33. FINAL ACCEPTANCE STANDARD

The final Gala Dock backend must be one platform, not a set of disconnected frontends.

A Customer can build and pay for an event using the same marketplace engines professionals use, without being forced into professional complexity.

An Organizer can run many simultaneous events, clients, suppliers, ticket sales, teams, promotion, money and live operations from a compact workspace.

A Provider can operate venues and/or services from one shell while retaining venue-specific and supplier-specific depth.

Tickets, maps, bookings, money, promotion, communications and reviews share canonical records.

Gala Agent can safely execute over those same records through typed, permissioned tools, including durable missions that wait and resume.

Admin can operate, support, reconcile and safeguard the platform without unrestricted unaudited private-data access.

API, MCP and webhooks expose governed capabilities without bypassing application permissions.

Every major asynchronous process is durable, idempotent, observable and retry-safe.

Every financial, booking and ticket lifecycle is deterministic and auditable.

Every release-critical system has tests, monitoring, recovery procedures and a defined owner.

**Do not stop at “implemented”. Complete the queue until the system is integrated, tested, hardened, documented and release-ready.**



# 16. DETAILED DOMAIN IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATIONS — 1–288

> **This section supersedes the short-name register as the implementation authority.** The register remains useful as an index, but Claude Code must implement and audit against the detailed card for every domain below. Do not mark a domain complete because its route renders or its table exists. A domain is complete only when its canonical state, permissions, UI, workflow, Agent/API integrations, failure handling, observability and tests all satisfy its card.

## 16.0 How to execute these cards

For each domain in queue order:

1. **Discover before writing.** Search routes, components, migrations, Supabase schema, RLS, server actions, Edge Functions, jobs, tests and docs for existing implementations and aliases.
2. **Choose the canonical model.** Reuse good records/services. Merge duplicate concepts. Write a migration/backfill plan before destructive changes.
3. **Define contracts.** Add typed commands, queries, schemas, errors, lifecycle/state transitions and domain events.
4. **Implement persistence.** Add/repair Supabase tables, constraints, indexes, triggers only where justified, RLS and transactional RPCs for atomic operations.
5. **Implement domain services.** Business rules belong in server/domain services; React, Agent, API, MCP and webhook handlers call those services rather than duplicating rules.
6. **Wire every consumer.** Connect Organizer, Provider, Customer, Admin, Public and Portals wherever the card specifies. Add loading, empty, error, permission-denied, degraded and success states.
7. **Wire Agent/API/MCP safely.** Read operations may be exposed broadly within scope; mutations require typed tools/scopes, idempotency and the same approval/authorization policy as human UI actions.
8. **Emit events.** Commit canonical state + audit + outbox event in the same database transaction for important mutations. Process downstream side effects asynchronously.
9. **Instrument.** Correlation IDs, structured errors, latency, success/failure counters and business-state metrics must exist before release.
10. **Test and prove.** Unit + integration + RLS + E2E + failure/retry + responsive/accessibility tests where the domain has UI. Never self-certify from code inspection only.

### Mandatory domain-card completion evidence
For each domain write/update `docs/backend/domains/<NNN>-<slug>.md` with: implementation location, schemas/tables, RLS policies, service entry points, routes/components, Agent tools, API/MCP scopes, events/jobs, test files, known limitations and release status.

---
## 1. Agent Tools

**Business purpose.** `Agent Tools` is a canonical Gala Dock backend domain, not a UI-only feature. It must own the rules and persisted state necessary for the capability to behave consistently across human UI, Gala Agent, API/MCP, background jobs and Admin operations. The implementation must favour one authoritative model over duplicate per-workspace copies and must preserve historical/audit evidence where commercial, safety or legal state is involved.

**Where it lives.** Gala Agent → Work plus contextual Agent actions throughout Organizer/Provider records. **Primary consumers:** Organizer Gala Agent; Provider Gala Agent; Platform Admin → Agent & Integrations. Hide irrelevant complexity by capability/role, but do not remove the underlying backend merely because one persona uses a simplified UI.

### 1.A Capability contract
- **1.1 Search Tools.** Provide permission-aware indexed discovery for **Search Tools**; support filters, pagination and deterministic empty/error states, and never return records the caller could not open directly.
- **1.2 Read Tools.** Implement **Read Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.3 Create Tools.** Create **Create Tools** through a validated command/service, assign tenant ownership, generate audit/outbox events and return the canonical persisted record rather than optimistic-only client state.
- **1.4 Update Tools.** Update **Update Tools** with field-level validation, optimistic concurrency/version checks and an auditable before/after change record; reject stale or unauthorised writes.
- **1.5 Delete Tools.** Implement **Delete Tools** using archive/soft-delete/anonymisation rules where business history must survive; hard deletion is reserved for legally eligible data and must respect retention/legal holds.
- **1.6 Archive Tools.** Archive **Archive Tools** without breaking financial/audit references; remove it from active defaults while preserving authorised historical retrieval and restore where policy allows.
- **1.7 Restore Tools.** Restore **Restore Tools** only when dependencies remain valid; re-run entitlement, uniqueness and lifecycle checks before returning a record to active state.
- **1.8 Batch Tools.** Implement **Batch Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.9 Compare Tools.** Implement **Compare Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.10 Calculate Tools.** Implement **Calculate Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.11 Forecast Tools.** Implement **Forecast Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.12 Optimisation Tools.** Implement **Optimisation Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.13 Communication Tools.** Implement **Communication Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.14 Marketplace Tools.** Implement **Marketplace Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.15 Booking Tools.** Implement **Booking Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.16 Ticket Tools.** Implement **Ticket Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.17 Finance Tools.** Implement **Finance Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.18 Map Tools.** Implement **Map Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.19 Media Tools.** Handle **Media Tools** through the canonical file/media service with tenant ownership, malware scanning, metadata, signed access, versioning/derivatives and storage lifecycle policies.
- **1.20 Calendar Tools.** Implement **Calendar Tools** using timezone-aware ranges and conflict detection; distinguish tentative holds, confirmed allocations, blackout periods and external-calendar information.
- **1.21 Team Tools.** Implement **Team Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.22 Sales Tools.** Implement **Sales Tools** as a first-class capability of **Agent Tools** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **1.23 Compliance Tools.** For **Compliance Tools**, distinguish submitted, pending, verified, failed, expired and manual-review states; retain source evidence privately and expose only accurate derived status publicly.
- **1.24 Reporting Tools.** Derive **Reporting Tools** from canonical event/ledger/activity data with documented metric definitions and time windows; avoid expensive ad-hoc scans against transactional tables.

### 1.B End-to-end behaviour
User or routine supplies a goal → resolve workspace, scope, permissions, plan and cost policy → select allowed skills/tools → execute read/draft actions → checkpoint mutations → pause for approvals/external waits → resume idempotently → validate results → write artifacts/audit/cost → present concise outcome and next action.

The flow must explicitly model **loading, draft, validation failure, permission denied, external dependency unavailable, partial success, retry, cancellation, stale-version conflict and completed** states where applicable. Never collapse `declined`, `unavailable`, `expired/no-response`, `failed` and `cancelled` into the same status.

### 1.C Supabase / data model
Treat these as **candidate canonical entities**, not permission to create duplicates: `agent_tools, agent_tool_versions, agent_tool_executions, agent_tool_permissions`. First inspect existing migrations and map equivalent tables. Add only the missing fields/tables.

For this domain:
- every tenant-owned row carries `workspace_id` or a verifiable parent relationship to a workspace/user;
- use UUID PKs, `created_at`, `updated_at`, actor/source metadata where material, and explicit lifecycle status rather than magic booleans;
- add foreign keys, unique constraints, CHECK constraints and exclusion/range constraints where they prevent invalid business state;
- add indexes from real query plans: workspace/status/date, parent/date, external provider IDs, geo/range fields and search keys as relevant;
- commercial commitments store **snapshots** of the accepted terms/prices/rules so later edits do not rewrite history;
- use JSONB only for genuinely variable provider payloads/configuration, not as a replacement for relational structure;
- important writes should insert an `audit_event` and `outbox_event` in the same transaction;
- concurrency-sensitive mutations use transaction-safe RPC/SQL constraints or optimistic version checks rather than “check then insert” client logic.

### 1.D RLS, authorization and privacy
Required permission model: agent.use, agent.run, agent.approve, agent.configure plus domain permissions inherited from the acting user.

Implement SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies separately. Test direct Supabase access with guessed IDs. Service-role use is restricted to trusted backend workers and must never become a shortcut for ordinary application authorization. Public projections expose only explicitly publishable fields. Sensitive files, payment data, verification evidence, private messages and operational contacts remain private even when the parent listing/event is public.

### 1.E Service and transaction design
Create or repair a typed **`agent_tools` domain service** with commands/queries that correspond to the capability list. Each mutation must:
1. resolve actor + workspace + entitlement;
2. validate input schema;
3. authorize the exact capability;
4. load/lock or version-check affected records;
5. enforce lifecycle/business rules;
6. commit canonical state atomically;
7. write audit/outbox/idempotency state where required;
8. enqueue slow/external side effects;
9. return a typed result/error contract.

Keep third-party SDK calls behind adapters. Do not call Stripe, Resend, map, AI or storage SDKs directly from React components.

### 1.F UI wiring and quality
Wire the backend into every relevant surface named above. UI requirements:
- use server-authoritative data for permissions, money, availability, inventory and verification;
- optimistic UI only for reversible low-risk edits and reconcile on failure;
- provide skeleton/loading, empty, first-use guidance, validation, inline error, global failure, degraded integration and success states;
- deep-link record IDs and filters; preserve browser Back/Forward;
- use drawers/modals for contained edits and canonical pages for records with ongoing lifecycle/activity;
- show **why** an action is disabled (permission, plan, state, missing verification, dependency or external outage);
- ensure desktop, tablet, mobile/PWA and keyboard/touch behaviour is coherent;

Explicitly handle:

- stale clients and concurrent edits;

- invalid lifecycle transition;

### 2.B End-to-end behaviour
User or routine supplies a goal → resolve workspace, scope, permissions, plan and cost policy → select allowed skills/tools → execute read/draft actions → checkpoint mutations → pause for approvals/external waits → resume idempotently → validate results → write artifacts/audit/cost → present concise outcome and next action.

The flow must explicitly model **loading, draft, validation failure, permission denied, external dependency unavailable, partial success, retry, cancellation, stale-version conflict and completed** states where applicable. Never collapse `declined`, `unavailable`, `expired/no-response`, `failed` and `cancelled` into the same status.

### 2.C Supabase / data model
Treat these as **candidate canonical entities**, not permission to create duplicates: `agent_skills, agent_skill_versions, agent_skill_tool_bindings, agent_skill_evaluations`. First inspect existing migrations and map equivalent tables. Add only the missing fields/tables.

For this domain:
- every tenant-owned row carries `workspace_id` or a verifiable parent relationship to a workspace/user;
- use UUID PKs, `created_at`, `updated_at`, actor/source metadata where material, and explicit lifecycle status rather than magic booleans;
- add foreign keys, unique constraints, CHECK constraints and exclusion/range constraints where they prevent invalid business state;
- add indexes from real query plans: workspace/status/date, parent/date, external provider IDs, geo/range fields and search keys as relevant;
- commercial commitments store **snapshots** of the accepted terms/prices/rules so later edits do not rewrite history;
- use JSONB only for genuinely variable provider payloads/configuration, not as a replacement for relational structure;
- important writes should insert an `audit_event` and `outbox_event` in the same transaction;
- concurrency-sensitive mutations use transaction-safe RPC/SQL constraints or optimistic version checks rather than “check then insert” client logic.

### 2.D RLS, authorization and privacy
Required permission model: agent.use, agent.run, agent.approve, agent.configure plus domain permissions inherited from the acting user.

Implement SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies separately. Test direct Supabase access with guessed IDs. Service-role use is restricted to trusted backend workers and must never become a shortcut for ordinary application authorization. Public projections expose only explicitly publishable fields. Sensitive files, payment data, verification evidence, private messages and operational contacts remain private even when the parent listing/event is public.

### 2.E Service and transaction design
Create or repair a typed **`agent_skills` domain service** with commands/queries that correspond to the capability list. Each mutation must:
1. resolve actor + workspace + entitlement;
2. validate input schema;
3. authorize the exact capability;
4. load/lock or version-check affected records;
5. enforce lifecycle/business rules;
6. commit canonical state atomically;
7. write audit/outbox/idempotency state where required;
8. enqueue slow/external side effects;
9. return a typed result/error contract.

Keep third-party SDK calls behind adapters. Do not call Stripe, Resend, map, AI or storage SDKs directly from React components.

Wire the backend into every relevant surface named above. UI requirements:
- use server-authoritative data for permissions, money, availability, inventory and verification;
- optimistic UI only for reversible low-risk edits and reconcile on failure;
- provide skeleton/loading, empty, first-use guidance, validation, inline error, global failure, degraded integration and success states;
- deep-link record IDs and filters; preserve browser Back/Forward;
- use drawers/modals for contained edits and canonical pages for records with ongoing lifecycle/activity;
- show **why** an action is disabled (permission, plan, state, missing verification, dependency or external outage);

## 5. Agent Runtime

**Where it lives.** Gala Agent → Work/History; Admin → Agent runtime health. **Primary consumers:** Organizer Gala Agent; Provider Gala Agent; Platform Admin → Agent & Integrations. Hide irrelevant complexity by capability/role, but do not remove the underlying backend merely because one persona uses a simplified UI.

### 5.A Capability contract
- **5.1 Run Queue.** Implement **Run Queue** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.2 Run Planner.** Implement **Run Planner** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.3 Run Steps.** Implement **Run Steps** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.4 Run State.** Treat **Run State** as an explicit state machine value with allowed transitions, actor/permission checks, preconditions, side effects and transition audit.
- **5.5 Run Checkpoints.** For **Run Checkpoints**, distinguish submitted, pending, verified, failed, expired and manual-review states; retain source evidence privately and expose only accurate derived status publicly.
- **5.6 Run Sleeps.** Implement **Run Sleeps** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.7 External Waits.** Implement **External Waits** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.

- **5.9 Parallel Steps.** Implement **Parallel Steps** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.10 Run Retries.** Implement **Run Retries** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.

- **5.14 Run Results.** Implement **Run Results** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **5.15 Run Artifacts.** Implement **Run Artifacts** as a first-class capability of **Agent Runtime** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.

### 5.B End-to-end behaviour
User or routine supplies a goal → resolve workspace, scope, permissions, plan and cost policy → select allowed skills/tools → execute read/draft actions → checkpoint mutations → pause for approvals/external waits → resume idempotently → validate results → write artifacts/audit/cost → present concise outcome and next action.

The flow must explicitly model **loading, draft, validation failure, permission denied, external dependency unavailable, partial success, retry, cancellation, stale-version conflict and completed** states where applicable. Never collapse `declined`, `unavailable`, `expired/no-response`, `failed` and `cancelled` into the same status.

### 5.C Supabase / data model
Treat these as **candidate canonical entities**, not permission to create duplicates: `agent_runs, agent_run_steps, agent_waits, agent_tool_executions, agent_artifacts, outbox_events`. First inspect existing migrations and map equivalent tables. Add only the missing fields/tables.

For this domain:
- every tenant-owned row carries `workspace_id` or a verifiable parent relationship to a workspace/user;
- use UUID PKs, `created_at`, `updated_at`, actor/source metadata where material, and explicit lifecycle status rather than magic booleans;
- add foreign keys, unique constraints, CHECK constraints and exclusion/range constraints where they prevent invalid business state;
- add indexes from real query plans: workspace/status/date, parent/date, external provider IDs, geo/range fields and search keys as relevant;
- commercial commitments store **snapshots** of the accepted terms/prices/rules so later edits do not rewrite history;
- use JSONB only for genuinely variable provider payloads/configuration, not as a replacement for relational structure;
- important writes should insert an `audit_event` and `outbox_event` in the same transaction;
- concurrency-sensitive mutations use transaction-safe RPC/SQL constraints or optimistic version checks rather than “check then insert” client logic.

### 5.D RLS, authorization and privacy
Required permission model: agent.use, agent.run, agent.approve, agent.configure plus domain permissions inherited from the acting user.

Implement SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies separately. Test direct Supabase access with guessed IDs. Service-role use is restricted to trusted backend workers and must never become a shortcut for ordinary application authorization. Public projections expose only explicitly publishable fields. Sensitive files, payment data, verification evidence, private messages and operational contacts remain private even when the parent listing/event is public.

### 5.E Service and transaction design
Create or repair a typed **`agent_runtime` domain service** with commands/queries that correspond to the capability list. Each mutation must:
1. resolve actor + workspace + entitlement;
2. validate input schema;
3. authorize the exact capability;
4. load/lock or version-check affected records;
5. enforce lifecycle/business rules;
6. commit canonical state atomically;
7. write audit/outbox/idempotency state where required;
8. enqueue slow/external side effects;
9. return a typed result/error contract.

Keep third-party SDK calls behind adapters. Do not call Stripe, Resend, map, AI or storage SDKs directly from React components.

### 5.F UI wiring and quality
Wire the backend into every relevant surface named above. UI requirements:
- use server-authoritative data for permissions, money, availability, inventory and verification;
- optimistic UI only for reversible low-risk edits and reconcile on failure;
- provide skeleton/loading, empty, first-use guidance, validation, inline error, global failure, degraded integration and success states;
- deep-link record IDs and filters; preserve browser Back/Forward;
- use drawers/modals for contained edits and canonical pages for records with ongoing lifecycle/activity;
- show **why** an action is disabled (permission, plan, state, missing verification, dependency or external outage);
- ensure desktop, tablet, mobile/PWA and keyboard/touch behaviour is coherent;
- add accessibility names, focus order, live-region feedback and reduced-motion behaviour as needed.

### 5.G Agent, API, MCP and automation
Expose safe reads and actions through the shared typed Tool Registry only when the user could perform the equivalent action manually. Agent tools inherit workspace/record permissions and risk level; consequential mutations go through approval policy. API/MCP scopes must be granular (`agent_runtime:read`, `agent_runtime:write`, plus narrower privileged scopes where needed). Batch/mission tools orchestrate lower-level commands and never bypass them.

Scheduled/event-driven behaviour must use the workflow/job infrastructure instead of browser timers. Watches sleep without consuming model tokens and wake from domain events or bounded polling.

### 5.H Domain events and background work
At minimum define events around creation/change/state transition/failure relevant to this domain, e.g. `agent_runtime.created`, `agent_runtime.updated`, `agent_runtime.state_changed`. Add narrower events for consequential child capabilities. Consumers must be idempotent and replay-safe. Heavy exports, notifications, indexing, media processing, matching, reconciliation and third-party delivery run asynchronously with retry/backoff/dead-letter handling.

### 5.I Failure, abuse and edge cases
Explicitly handle:
- duplicate requests/webhooks/actions;
- stale clients and concurrent edits;
- deleted/revoked membership during a flow;
- external provider timeout or ambiguous outcome;
- partial batch success;
- invalid lifecycle transition;
- expired holds/tokens/links where relevant;
- account/workspace suspension;
- data retained for audit after user-facing cancellation/deletion;
- malicious input/file content and prompt injection if data can reach Gala Agent;
- accessibility and timezone/currency/locale edge cases.

### 5.J Observability and operational quality
Instrument correlation IDs and measure success/failure/latency plus domain-relevant business metrics. suspend idle runs; retrieve scoped context only; checkpoint after side effects; cache deterministic reads; bound concurrency. Add structured logs with secrets/PII redaction, alerts for repeated failures and an Admin/operations diagnostic path for stuck asynchronous work.

### 5.K Tests and acceptance gates
Minimum domain-specific focus: tool-contract tests, mission replay, approval boundaries, restart durability, prompt-injection suites, cost-cap tests, cross-tenant denial. Also require:
- unit tests for validators/calculations/state transitions;
- repository/service integration tests against Supabase;
- positive + negative RLS tests;
- E2E happy path plus at least one failure/recovery path;
- duplicate/idempotency and concurrency test for consequential mutations;
- Agent tool permission/approval test where exposed;
- API/MCP scope test where exposed;
- visual/responsive/accessibility checks for all user-facing routes.

**Done only when:** the feature is persisted, permission-safe, reachable from the intended UI, usable without console/manual DB intervention, wired to dependent domains, observable, documented and backed by passing automated evidence. A rendered screen or existing table alone is not completion.

- **8.5 Provider Context.** Implement **Provider Context** as a first-class capability of **Agent Context** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **8.6 Venue Context.** Implement **Venue Context** as a first-class capability of **Agent Context** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **8.7 Finance Context.** Implement **Finance Context** as a first-class capability of **Agent Context** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **8.8 Calendar Context.** Implement **Calendar Context** using timezone-aware ranges and conflict detection; distinguish tentative holds, confirmed allocations, blackout periods and external-calendar information.
- **8.9 Historical Context.** Implement **Historical Context** as a first-class capability of **Agent Context** with a typed service contract, persisted canonical state, permission checks, audit/events, clear UI loading/empty/error states and integration tests.
- **8.10 Permission Context.** Define **Permission Context** as explicit server-side capabilities, not UI labels; combine role grants, record scope, workspace membership and step-up/approval requirements.

### 8.B End-to-end behaviour
User or routine supplies a goal → resolve workspace, scope, permissions, plan and cost policy → select allowed skills/tools → execute read/draft actions → checkpoint mutations → pause for approvals/external waits → resume idempotently → validate results → write artifacts/audit/cost → present concise outcome and next action.

The flow must explicitly model **loading, draft, validation failure, permission denied, external dependency unavailable, partial success, retry, cancellation, stale-version conflict and completed** states where applicable. Never collapse `declined`, `unavailable`, `expired/no-response`, `failed` and `cancelled` into the same status.

### 8.C Supabase / data model
Treat these as **candidate canonical entities**, not permission to create duplicates: `agent_threads, agent_runs, agent_run_steps, agent_tool_executions, agent_skills, agent_approvals, agent_routines, agent_waits, agent_artifacts, ai_credit_ledger`. First inspect existing migrations and map equivalent tables. Add only the missing fields/tables.

For this domain:
- every tenant-owned row carries `workspace_id` or a verifiable parent relationship to a workspace/user;
- use UUID PKs, `created_at`, `updated_at`, actor/source metadata where material, and explicit lifecycle status rather than magic booleans;
- add foreign keys, unique constraints, CHECK constraints and exclusion/range constraints where they prevent invalid business state;
- add indexes from real query plans: workspace/status/date, parent/date, external provider IDs, geo/range fields and search keys as relevant;
- commercial commitments store **snapshots** of the accepted terms/prices/rules so later edits do not rewrite history;
- use JSONB only for genuinely variable provider payloads/configuration, not as a replacement for relational structure;
- important writes should insert an `audit_event` and `outbox_event` in the same transaction;
- concurrency-sensitive mutations use transaction-safe RPC/SQL constraints or optimistic version checks rather than “check then insert” client logic.

### 8.D RLS, authorization and privacy
Required permission model: agent.use, agent.run, agent.approve, agent.configure plus domain permissions inherited from the acting user.

Implement SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies separately. Test direct Supabase access with guessed IDs. Service-role use is restricted to trusted backend workers and must never become a shortcut for ordinary application authorization. Public projections expose only explicitly publishable fields. Sensitive files, payment data, verification evidence, private messages and operational contacts remain private even when the parent listing/event is public.

### 8.E Service and transaction design
Create or repair a typed **`agent_context` domain service** with commands/queries that correspond to the capability list. Each mutation must:
1. resolve actor + workspace + entitlement;
2. validate input schema;
3. authorize the exact capability;
4. load/lock or version-check affected records;
5. enforce lifecycle/business rules;
6. commit canonical state atomically;
7. write audit/outbox/idempotency state where required;
8. enqueue slow/external side effects;
9. return a typed result/error contract.

Keep third-party SDK calls behind adapters. Do not call Stripe, Resend, map, AI or storage SDKs directly from React components.

### 8.F UI wiring and quality
Wire the backend into every relevant surface named above. UI requirements:
- use server-authoritative data for permissions, money, availability, inventory and verification;
- optimistic UI only for reversible low-risk edits and reconcile on failure;
- provide skeleton/loading, empty, first-use guidance, validation, inline error, global failure, degraded integration and success states;
- deep-link record IDs and filters; preserve browser Back/Forward;
- use drawers/modals for contained edits and canonical pages for records with ongoing lifecycle/activity;
- show **why** an action is disabled (permission, plan, state, missing verification, dependency or external outage);
- ensure desktop, tablet, mobile/PWA and keyboard/touch behaviour is coherent;
- add accessibility names, focus order, live-region feedback and reduced-motion behaviour as needed.

### 8.G Agent, API, MCP and automation
Expose safe reads and actions through the shared typed Tool Registry only when the user could perform the equivalent action manually. Agent tools inherit workspace/record permissions and risk level; consequential mutations go through approval policy. API/MCP scopes must be granular (`agent_context:read`, `agent_context:write`, plus narrower privileged scopes where needed). Batch/mission tools orchestrate lower-level commands and never bypass them.

Scheduled/event-driven behaviour must use the workflow/job infrastructure instead of browser timers. Watches sleep without consuming model tokens and wake from domain events or bounded polling.

### 8.H Domain events and background work
At minimum define events around creation/change/state transition/failure relevant to this domain, e.g. `agent_context.created`, `agent_context.updated`, `agent_context.state_changed`. Add narrower events for consequential child capabilities. Consumers must be idempotent and replay-safe. Heavy exports, notifications, indexing, media processing, matching, reconciliation and third-party delivery run asynchronously with retry/backoff/dead-letter handling.

### 8.I Failure, abuse and edge cases
Explicitly handle:
- duplicate requests/webhooks/actions;
- stale clients and concurrent edits;
- deleted/revoked membership during a flow;
- external provider timeout or ambiguous outcome;
- partial batch success;
- invalid lifecycle transition;
- expired holds/tokens/links where relevant;
- account/workspace suspension;
- data retained for audit after user-facing cancellation/deletion;
- malicious input/file content and prompt injection if data can reach Gala Agent;
- accessibility and timezone/currency/locale edge cases.

### 8.J Observability and operational quality
Instrument correlation IDs and measure success/failure/latency plus domain-relevant business metrics. suspend idle runs; retrieve scoped context only; checkpoint after side effects; cache deterministic reads; bound concurrency. Add structured logs with secrets/PII redaction, alerts for repeated failures and an Admin/operations diagnostic path for stuck asynchronous work.

### 8.K Tests and acceptance gates
Minimum domain-specific focus: tool-contract tests, mission replay, approval boundaries, restart durability, prompt-injection suites, cost-cap tests, cross-tenant denial. Also require:
- unit tests for validators/calculations/state transitions;
- repository/service integration tests against Supabase;
- positive + negative RLS tests;
- E2E happy path plus at least one failure/recovery path;
- duplicate/idempotency and concurrency test for consequential mutations;
- Agent tool permission/approval test where exposed;
- API/MCP scope test where exposed;
- visual/responsive/accessibility checks for all user-facing routes.

**Done only when:** the feature is persisted, permission-safe, reachable from the intended UI, usable without console/manual DB intervention, wired to dependent domains, observable, documented and backed by passing automated evidence. A rendered screen or existing table alone is not completion.

**Dependency note.** 16–31 foundation/workflow, the domain services the Agent is allowed to operate, 189–194 integration controls, 206–218 security/observability

- use JSONB only for genuinely variable provider payloads/configuration, not as a replacement for relational structure;
- important writes should insert an `audit_event` and `outbox_event` in the same transaction;
- concurrency-sensitive mutations use transaction-safe RPC/SQL constraints or optimistic version checks rather than “check then insert” client logic.

### 11.D RLS, authorization and privacy
Required permission model: agent.use, agent.run, agent.approve, agent.configure plus domain permissions inherited from the acting user.

Implement SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies separately. Test direct Supabase access with guessed IDs. Service-role use is restricted to trusted backend workers and must never become a shortcut for ordinary application authorization. Public projections expose only explicitly publishable fields. Sensitive files, payment data, verification evidence, private messages and operational contacts remain private even when the parent listing/event is public.

### 11.E Service and transaction design
Create or repair a typed **`agent_routing` domain service** with commands/queries that correspond to the capability list. Each mutation must:
1. resolve actor + workspace + entitlement;
2. validate input schema;
3. authorize the exact capability;
4. load/lock or version-check affected records;
5. enforce lifecycle/business rules;
6. commit canonical state atomically;
7. write audit/outbox/idempotency state where required;
8. enqueue slow/external side effects;
9. return a typed result/error contract.

Keep third-party SDK calls behind adapters. Do not call Stripe, Resend, map, AI or storage SDKs directly from React components.

### 11.F UI wiring and quality
Wire the backend into every relevant surface named above. UI requirements:
- use server-authoritative data for permissions, money, availability, inventory and verification;
- optimistic UI only for reversible low-risk edits and reconcile on failure;
- provide skeleton/loading, empty, first-use guidance, validation, inline error, global failure, degraded integration and success states;
- deep-link record IDs and filters; preserve browser Back/Forward;
- use drawers/modals for contained edits and canonical pages for records with ongoing lifecycle/activity;
- show **why** an action is disabled (permission, plan, state, missing verification, dependency or external outage);
- ensure desktop, tablet, mobile/PWA and keyboard/touch behaviour is coherent;
- add accessibility names, focus order, live-region feedback and reduced-motion behaviour as needed.

### 11.G Agent, API, MCP and automation
Expose safe reads and actions through the shared typed Tool Registry only when the user could perform the equivalent action manually. Agent tools inherit workspace/record permissions and risk level; consequential mutations go through approval policy. API/MCP scopes must be granular (`agent_routing:read`, `agent_routing:write`, plus narrower privileged scopes where needed). Batch/mission tools orchestrate lower-level commands and never bypass them.

Scheduled/event-driven behaviour must use the workflow/job infrastructure instead of browser timers. Watches sleep without consuming model tokens and wake from domain events or bounded polling.

### 11.H Domain events and background work
At minimum define events around creation/change/state transition/failure relevant to this domain, e.g. `agent_routing.created`, `agent_routing.updated`, `agent_routing.state_changed`. Add narrower events for consequential child capabilities. Consumers must be idempotent and replay-safe. Heavy exports, notifications, indexing, media processing, matching, reconciliation and third-party delivery run asynchronously with retry/backoff/dead-letter handling.

### 11.I Failure, abuse and edge cases
Explicitly handle:
- duplicate requests/webhooks/actions;
- stale clients and concurrent edits;
- deleted/revoked membership during a flow;
- external provider timeout or ambiguous outcome;
- partial batch success;
- invalid lifecycle transition;
- expired holds/tokens/links where relevant;
- account/workspace suspension;
- data retained for audit after user-facing cancellation/deletion;
- malicious input/file content and prompt injection if data can reach Gala Agent;
- accessibility and timezone/currency/locale edge cases.

### 11.J Observability and operational quality
Instrument correlation IDs and measure success/failure/latency plus domain-relevant business metrics. suspend idle runs; retrieve scoped context only; checkpoint after side effects; cache deterministic reads; bound concurrency. Add structured logs with secrets/PII redaction, alerts for repeated failures and an Admin/operations diagnostic path for stuck asynchronous work.

### 11.K Tests and acceptance gates
Minimum domain-specific focus: tool-contract tests, mission replay, approval boundaries, restart durability, prompt-injection suites, cost-cap tests, cross-tenant denial. Also require:
- unit tests for validators/calculations/state transitions;
- repository/service integration tests against Supabase;
- positive + negative RLS tests;
- E2E happy path plus at least one failure/recovery path;
- duplicate/idempotency and concurrency test for consequential mutations;
- Agent tool permission/approval test where exposed;
- API/MCP scope test where exposed;
- visual/responsive/accessibility checks for all user-facing routes.

**Done only when:** the feature is persisted, permission-safe, reachable from the intended UI, usable without console/manual DB intervention, wired to dependent domains, observable, documented and backed by passing automated evidence. A rendered screen or existing table alone is not completion.

**Dependency note.** 16–31 foundation/workflow, the domain services the Agent is allowed to operate, 189–194 integration controls, 206–218 security/observability

## 12. Agent Economics

**Business purpose.** `Agent Economics` is a canonical Gala Dock backend domain, not a UI-only feature. It must own the rules and persisted state necessary for the capability to behave consistently across human UI, Gala Agent, API/MCP, background jobs and Admin operations. - ensure desktop, tablet, mobile/PWA and keyboard/touch behaviour is coherent;
- add accessibility names, focus order, live-region feedback and reduced-motion behaviour as needed.

### 14.G Agent, API, MCP and automation
Expose safe reads and actions through the shared typed Tool Registry only when the user could perform the equivalent action manually. Agent tools inherit workspace/record permissions and risk level; consequential mutations go through approval policy. API/MCP scopes must be granular (`agent_evaluation:read`, `agent_evaluation:write`, plus narrower privileged scopes where needed). Batch/mission tools orchestrate lower-level commands and never bypass them.

Scheduled/event-driven behaviour must use the workflow/job infrastructure instead of browser timers. Watches sleep without consuming model tokens and wake from domain events or bounded polling.

### 14.H Domain events and background work
At minimum define events around creation/change/state transition/failure relevant to this domain, e.g. `agent_evaluation.created`, `agent_evaluation.updated`, `agent_evaluation.state_changed`. Add narrower events for consequential child capabilities. Consumers must be idempotent and replay-safe. Heavy exports, notifications, indexing, media processing, matching, reconciliation and third-party delivery run asynchronously with retry/backoff/dead-letter handling.

### 14.I Failure, abuse and edge cases
Explicitly handle:
- duplicate requests/webhooks/actions;
- stale clients and concurrent edits;
- deleted/revoked membership during a flow;
- external provider timeout or ambiguous outcome;
- partial batch success;
- invalid lifecycle transition;
- expired holds/tokens/links where relevant;
- account/workspace suspension;
- data retained for audit after user-facing cancellation/deletion;
- malicious input/file content and prompt injection if data can reach Gala Agent;
- accessibility and timezone/currency/locale edge cases.

### 14.J Observability and operational quality
Instrument correlation IDs and measure success/failure/latency plus domain-relevant business metrics. suspend idle runs; retrieve scoped context only; checkpoint after side effects; cache deterministic reads; bound concurrency. Add structured logs with secrets/PII redaction, alerts for repeated failures and an Admin/operations diagnostic path for stuck asynchronous work.

### 14.K Tests and acceptance gates
Minimum domain-specific focus: tool-contract tests, mission replay, approval boundaries, restart durability, prompt-injection suites, cost-cap tests, cross-tenant denial. Also require:
- unit tests for validators/calculations/state transitions;
- repository/service integration tests against Supabase;
- positive + negative RLS tests;
- E2E happy path plus at least one failure/recovery path;
- duplicate/idempotency and concurrency test for consequential mutations;
- Agent tool permission/approval test where exposed;
- API/MCP scope test where exposed;
- visual/responsive/accessibility checks for all user-facing routes.

**Done only when:** the feature is persisted, permission-safe, reachable from the intended UI, usable without console/manual DB intervention, wired to dependent domains, observable, documented and backed by passing automated evidence. A rendered screen or existing table alone is not completion.

**Dependency note.** 16–31 foundation/workflow, the domain services the Agent is allowed to operate, 189–194 integration controls, 206–218 security/observability
